dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The cluster contains 17 annual renewals totaling $1,506.29: DLR-104 has 8/$723.42 and DLR-219 has 9/$782.87." Source: "recharges.csv"

"Both batches reconcile exactly: rows received equal rows accepted (8 and 9), duplicate source IDs are zero, cash equals ledger, differences are $0, and status is RECONCILED." Source: "dealer_import_log.csv, DF-00020 and DF-00040"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Posting-date reporting concentrates prior activity into the final May week... Posting lags range from 3–30 days."
"The 31 May cluster is consistent with controlled month-end batching by DLR-104 and DLR-219."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Manipulated reporting: rejected on current evidence."
"The dealer contracts, dealer-name/West-region mapping, entitlement ledger, and settlement evidence were not supplied."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Produce a reversible shadow version of the weekly trend pack that allocates these 17 renewals by effective_event_date and labels them ‘late dealer batch,’ while preserving posted_at."
"Reconcile the two source files to entitlement and settlement records—including the UPI-coded item—then close the case if those checks remain clean."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "No material revenue issue; do not escalate as duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, or a pipeline defect."
"One DLR-219 record—EVT-0000007097, $97.59—is coded UPI... This may only reflect a broad control-label definition, but it should be confirmed."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Monthly submission is contractually permitted" is supported only by the dealer email; the submission explicitly acknowledges that the contract was not supplied.

"do not escalate as ... manipulated reporting, or a pipeline defect" is somewhat broader than the evidence: the checks strongly address duplicate ingestion and batch-control failure, but do not fully exclude intentional reporting manipulation or defects elsewhere in the pipeline.
"cash equals ledger" and the conclusion that there is no material revenue issue remain conditional because entitlement and settlement evidence were not yet tested.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A real entitlement or settlement duplication could still exist outside the supplied recharge and dealer-import controls, or the pattern could reflect unauthorized batching rather than a benign posting convention. The analyst identified these possibilities and named decision-changing evidence, but did not yet test them.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete and document the entitlement-and-settlement join for all 17 renewals, including the UPI-coded item, with explicit checks for prior recognition, duplicate entitlement, and settled cash before closing the case.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South monthly cases fell from 197 in April to 128 in June."
"South IVR-origin cases fell only 10.3% pre/post, while agent-direct and app cases fell 42.1% and 43.8%."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "This is consistent with improvement, but does not establish it: the reduction is concentrated in non-IVR case origins and could reflect routing, case-creation, or reporting changes."
"Case counts are a demand and measurement signal, not a satisfaction, resolution, or repeat-contact metric."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Fewer recorded complaints are not yet evidence of improved self-service or customer experience."
"Material unknowns: pilot launch date and eligible population; IVR completion, abandonment, transfer, and fallback-to-agent rates; changes to case-routing/source tagging/deduplication."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet."
"Keep the South pilot running, but do not scale nationally. Randomize or phase-rollout eligible customers with a holdout."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Measure cases per active subscriber, IVR completion/abandonment/agent transfer, 7/30-day repeat contacts, resolution/reopen rates, and CSAT."
"For a representative sample of IVR exits, what evidence distinguishes successful self-service from abandonment, failed authentication, or an unresolved issue routed elsewhere?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The quantitative breakdowns by case origin and region are cited only to whole files, without specifying the relevant fields, date windows, filters, or reproducible calculation; their definitions therefore cannot be independently verified from the submission alone.

"South recorded affected accounts in service events were higher in June ... despite lower case volume" is an observation, but it does not establish comparable customer exposure or that service events should move one-for-one with complaints.
The wording "Fewer recorded complaints" risks treating ticket cases as complaints, even though the submission otherwise correctly describes cases as a measurement signal.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handles the strongest measurement alternatives—case-creation failure, routing, source tagging, deduplication, and reporting changes—and recognizes that IVR abandonment is not necessarily a complaint. It does not fully develop the benign interpretation that the pilot may have improved some customer journeys while unrelated non-IVR case volumes fell, nor does it show whether the service-event comparison represents comparable exposure.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and analyze a timestamped, end-to-end South IVR funnel linked to eligible customers and downstream cases—especially pre-case errors, abandonment, transfers, fallback-to-agent, repeat contacts, and sampled call outcomes—before attributing the case decline to NovaIVR or expanding it.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites inverter_events.csv row 2 for the seven-minute COMM_LINK_WARN, 0 MW impact, and clearance.
It cites inverter_events.csv rows 2–5 for the four distinct inverters/event types, clearance, and zero reported impact.
It appropriately limits the claim to “this extract” and states that it cannot establish plant-wide normality.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission distinguishes a brief, cleared communications warning from a systemic failure and checks recurrence/nonzero impact as decision-changing evidence.
It uses the event records to reject repetition and production-loss explanations, but relies primarily on one data source rather than triangulating independent operational channels.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It states “high confidence for the file; low confidence plant-wide,” clearly separating observed extract-level evidence from broader uncertainty.
It identifies the smallest useful follow-up: checking INV-17 communication events/status for plus or minus 24 hours, with recurrence or nonzero impact as escalation triggers.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation—“one cheap check—not escalation”—is proportionate to the seven-minute, zero-impact, cleared warning.
It provides a discriminating follow-up and a clear stopping rule: “otherwise stop—do not escalate from this file alone.”

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion that the extract does not demonstrate systemic inverter failure or production loss is accurately scoped to the supplied records.
The submission follows the evidence and matches the appropriate low-escalation response without inventing a plant problem from a communications warning.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: No material unsupported claim is apparent. The statement that no broader incident pattern appears is appropriately limited to the extract, although the analysis does not independently verify plant-wide status.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A transient communications or telemetry interruption affecting INV-17, with no demonstrated production effect, is more consistent with the brief cleared warning and 0 MW impact than a systemic inverter failure. The available extract cannot fully distinguish that from a short-lived status-reporting anomaly.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: If readily available, cross-check INV-17’s communication/status record against an independent operational or power-output channel over the same plus-or-minus 24-hour window; otherwise retain the stated stopping point.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: “28 May: Rs 662,444.09” versus “29 May: Rs 453,085.88,” with the 31.60% calculation shown.
“Sum of abs(submitted schedule - actual) x 0.25 h: 378.99 versus 282.76 MWh.”
“29 May counterfactual: approximately Rs 549,569 base versus Rs 453,086 submitted.”
The submission identifies the CSV as containing submitted schedules rather than confirmed accepted schedules or audited settlement data.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: It distinguishes the day-to-day comparison from the same-day base-versus-submitted counterfactual.
It tests recorded alternatives including “same firmware 4.7, 98.5% availability, zero curtailment, 10 stow blocks” and comparable wind and DSM-rate measures.
It checks the 4 June record and notes that it has a lower penalty but “is not a clean comparator.”
It identifies the remaining Rs 112,875 as differences between days that are “causally unidentified.”

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “Does not establish that the pilot caused a 31.6% reduction.”
The narrower result is explicitly described as “an ex-post mechanical comparison” and “not an estimate of expected future causal impact.”
It states that acceptance, final settlement, random assignment, and sampling uncertainty are not established.
It distinguishes modeled penalty from final billed savings.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: The submission preserves the smaller same-day benefit rather than dismissing the pilot: “lowered the modelled penalty by approximately Rs 96,483 (17.6%).”
It identifies decision-relevant missing evidence: “accepted-schedule record, settlement invoice,” and additional comparable observations.
The submission does not provide a fully explicit prospective decision rule or a clearly specified next discriminating test.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: “The evidence reproduces a 31.6% observed reduction, but does not establish that the pilot caused a 31.6% reduction.”
It retains the conditional same-day result: “12 pilot-labelled schedule revisions lowered the modelled penalty” by approximately Rs 96,483.
It correctly attributes only about 46% of the day-to-day difference mechanically and leaves the remainder unidentified.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The comparison days are similar on recorded controls” is supported for the listed controls, but it should not be read as establishing overall comparability; unmeasured weather, forecast, dispatch, and market conditions may still differ materially.

“Availability, curtailment, firmware, or recorded rate-count differences explain the comparison: rejected as primary explanations because these are equal across 28-29 May” is reasonable for those measured variables, but equality alone does not rule out other operational or market explanations.

The statement that revisions “lowered” penalty is valid as a modeled fixed-actual-generation counterfactual, not as evidence of realized settlement savings; the submission largely makes this qualification explicit.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Most of the Rs 209,358 day-to-day difference may reflect weather, forecast accuracy, dispatch, market conditions, or other differences between 28 and 29 May. The same-day base-versus-submitted calculation supports a smaller conditional mechanical benefit, but not a repeatable causal effect or final commercial saving.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain the accepted schedules and final settlement records for multiple matched high-wind events, then pre-specify a prospective or matched-event comparison of base versus pilot schedules. This would test both whether the revisions are actually accepted and whether the modeled same-day benefit survives settlement and generalizes beyond 29 May.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The accepted Swiss declaration uses 90211000 for P1001, U.S. origin, on 2025-11-04."
"The Swiss matrix assigns P1001 to 90211000, effective 2025-01-01, with no end date."
"Helios lists 90211090, but the shared base HS6 is 902110."
"Invoice product, manufacturing country, and CHF 126,900 line value agree with the declaration; the AWB links the same packet."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses"
"Different final digits prove misclassification: rejected because Swiss and Helios/EU nomenclatures need not use identical eight-digit strings."
"Helios is controlling: rejected because it is commercial master data, its snapshot postdates the declaration, and it is not a legal-ruling source."
"90211000 is unsupported: rejected because it exactly matches the effective Swiss working classification."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "with medium-high confidence"
"An official Tares extract or product-specific Swiss ruling effective 2025-11-04, including nomenclature version and classification rationale, could materially change the conclusion."
"The supplied schema does not capture those attributes."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "The matrix expressly says Switzerland uses local tariff codes and cross-jurisdiction string matches are not expected."
"Helios is commercial master data, may use migration mappings, and is not an effective-dated customs-ruling history."
"Do not amend the accepted declaration solely to match Helios."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Close the automated flag as not a likely declaration error, document the jurisdictional mapping, and ask the Swiss trade owner or broker to confirm 90211000 against contemporaneous Tares/ruling evidence."
"Do not amend the accepted declaration solely to match Helios."
"Separately investigate the invoice’s quantity/unit-value arithmetic inconsistency; it concerns valuation, not this code decision."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Separately investigate the invoice’s quantity/unit-value arithmetic inconsistency" is asserted without showing the arithmetic or identifying the relevant invoice fields.
"The AWB links the same packet" is not explained with a specific airway-bill identifier or matching field, although the cited AWB may support it.

The conclusion treats the Swiss matrix as an "effective Swiss working classification" without establishing that it is legally authoritative; the submission appropriately mitigates this by requesting contemporaneous Tares or ruling confirmation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Helios 90211090 could reflect a product-specific, updated, or legally controlling classification, while the Swiss matrix could be generic, stale, or nonbinding. Without the contemporaneous Tares extract, nomenclature version, and classification rationale, a declaration error cannot be ruled out completely despite the strong jurisdiction-mismatch explanation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide the exact relevant matrix, declaration, invoice, and AWB fields—or an official contemporaneous Tares/ruling extract—and show the invoice arithmetic supporting the separate valuation concern.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Preference was claimed for P1006, with declared origin United States, 0.0% duty, and status “Accepted.”" tied to "Customs declaration IE-2025-000411, dated 2025-09-18".
"Invoice data matches the declaration: P1006 spinal fixation rod, EUR 193,400, manufacturing country United States." tied to "Commercial invoice INV-000411".
"The only SUP-02/P1006 entry covers 2025-01-01 through 2025-07-31, states Ireland, and is marked “Expired in register.”" tied to "Supplier origin register".
"The search result expressly says this does not prove that no document exists outside the register."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Preference: Yes,’ 0.0% duty, or ‘Accepted’ proves eligibility." is explicitly rejected because "These fields show the declaration outcome, not the documentary or rules-of-origin basis."
"The invoice’s United States manufacturing country proves preferential origin" is rejected because "Manufacturing country is not, by itself, evidence that a preferential-origin rule was satisfied."
"The AWB’s Ireland route proves Irish origin" is rejected because "It describes transport routing, not production or origin qualification."
"No current register result proves no declaration exists" is rejected with the limitation that "supporting documents may exist outside the register."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The preferential-origin claim ... is not supported by the evidence currently available. This is an evidence gap, not proof that the claim is invalid."

The evidence table distinguishes confidence that records reflect filed or transactional facts from confidence that they prove entitlement: "High that this records what was filed; low that it proves entitlement" and "High for transaction matching; low as preferential-origin proof."
"Do not approve or rely on the preference claim until valid supplier support and the applicable origin rule are obtained and verified."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Internal workshop notes distinguish manufacturing-country data from preference proof and identify the supplier declaration and applied origin rule as necessary."
The submission identifies a data-lineage limitation: "the register may be incomplete."
The proposed workflow is explicit: "Validate its supplier, product, shipment, origin, and validity period before linking it in ClearView."

It recognizes that the recorded 0.0% rate may have different system or legal bases: "Confirmation whether the 0.0% rate resulted from preference or from an independently applicable ordinary tariff rate."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place the preference claim on documentary hold" rather than declaring it invalid.
"Request the current supplier declaration ... together with the rule and qualification calculation used by the broker."

"If adequate evidence cannot be produced, do not affirm the preference claim; have the authorized customs owner assess non-preferential treatment and any required amendment to the accepted declaration."
The action includes controlled validation before system use: "before linking it in ClearView."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: No material unsupported conclusion is apparent. The statement "The only SUP-02/P1006 entry" depends on the completeness of the searched register, but the submission expressly qualifies the result by stating that documents may exist outside the register.
The source citations identify files and documents but generally do not provide page, row, or field-level references; this is a minor traceability limitation rather than an evidentiary overstatement.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference may still be valid because the register is incomplete, the supplier declaration may exist outside it, or the 0.0% rate may arise from an independently applicable ordinary tariff rate. The submission appropriately treats these as unresolved possibilities rather than proof of invalidity.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add page-, row-, or field-level citations and obtain the supplier declaration plus the specific preferential arrangement, product rule, and qualification calculation so entitlement can be tested rather than only placed on hold.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "181 of 215 releases occur at exactly 02:10:00, across all four sites" — tied to batch_release.csv and source_freshness.csv.
"The 215 released batches have a median receipt-to-release interval of 39.0 hours" — tied to batch_release.csv rows 2–221.
"LabTrack is reported current only through 2026-07-29 23:00, yet 11 records contain later lab_complete_ts values" — tied to source_freshness.csv and named batch rows.
The submission distinguishes observations from inferences, e.g. flags are "verification triggers, not proof of noncompliance."

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "This is not the SOP metric: QL-204 defines the target as 24 hours from required evidence available to disposition" separates the measured symptom from the contractual clock.
"The release timestamp also appears potentially system-generated" links the 02:10 concentration to a timestamp-semantics hypothesis without treating it as proven.
The submission tests alternatives including lab completion as the start, genuine overnight disposition work, timezone differences, and snapshot-state explanations for flags.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "needs verification before treating it as the authorized disposition time" appropriately limits the timestamp conclusion.
"Medium—flags may describe snapshot state rather than state at disposition" is claim-specific calibration.
"Until this passes, report the 39-hour figure only as a receipt-to-recorded-disposition interval—unvalidated" converts uncertainty into an operational reporting boundary.
The submission identifies missing timestamp definitions, timezone metadata, lineage, and non-coherent source timing as decision-relevant uncertainties.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not use the apparent cycle time as a performance KPI yet" directly changes the proposed decision rather than accepting the apparent metric.
It proposes a small, reversible verification using one clean 02:10 batch and specifies the reconciliation checks required before KPI approval.
It preserves a useful interim measure by labeling the 39-hour value as an unvalidated recorded-disposition interval rather than discarding it or misusing it.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Use lab_complete_ts as evidence-ready time. Rejected" because the SOP requires additional certificate, deviation, exception, and market checks.
"The 02:10 pattern merely reflects genuine overnight disposition work. Possible, but not credible enough to assume" identifies and bounds a strong competing explanation.
"Missing COAs and open deviations prove improper releases. Not established" rejects an unsafe compliance inference and states plausible alternatives.
"Timezone differences explain the freshness conflict. Possible, but the files provide no timezone metadata" identifies what remains unresolved.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Smallest verification: trace one clean 02:10 batch" is a prioritized, high-value next query.

The requested checks—authorized-disposition timestamp, timezone, final required-evidence availability, and reconciliation to qcore_release_ts—directly discriminate workflow delay from interface timing.
The additional requests for catalog definitions, lineage, evidence-ready timestamp, classification, exception intervals, and dashboard scope are tied to explicit KPI decision gates.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that qcore_release_ts "may be a batch/interface timestamp" is a well-supported hypothesis, not a demonstrated fact; the 02:10 concentration alone cannot establish its origin.
The stated 39.0-hour median and row-level counts are presented as calculations from the extracts, but the submission does not show the calculation method or distribution beyond the cited totals.
The assertion that all 42 HOLD records are Riverbend records is traceable as reported, but its operational significance is limited because source-snapshot coherence is not established.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 concentration could reflect genuine overnight authorized dispositions, a scheduled batch process, or timezone/reporting conventions rather than an interface-timestamp artifact. The proposed QCore audit-history check and timestamp/timezone reconciliation are the right tests to distinguish these explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and reconcile the QCore audit history for one representative 02:10 batch with the final required-evidence event, including explicit timezone and event-type definitions; use the result to decide whether the entire KPI should be redefined or merely relabeled.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The 24 requests represent $166,495.60" and "assuming external_quote_usd is a unit price"; cites part_requests.csv rows 2–25.
"Exact-spec candidate pool is $38,385.77"; cites part_requests.csv, spare_parts.csv, and part_restrictions.csv, with specific spare-parts row ranges.
"MaintStar-global is dated 2026-06-26"; triangulates source_freshness (1).csv row 6 with maintenance_email.txt Image 4 and the request export date.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Proceed with a semantic-search pilot as a candidate generator, but do not authorize transfers or recognize savings from this extract."
"Candidate values are not additive; several requests compete for the same actuator and belt units."
"Description similarity is discovery evidence, not equivalence" and the analysis separately applies revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, and freshness gates.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Medium: arithmetic is exact, but quote-unit semantics need confirmation" and "Medium" confidence for the exact-spec candidate pool.
"The snapshot-based opportunity ceiling is therefore $46,582.61 ... it is not yet bankable savings."
The claim "No transfer is actionable now because donor stock is stale" is appropriately conservative operationally, but stale data alone does not establish that every candidate is unavailable.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: Reframes the task from immediate savings recognition to a "semantic-search pilot as a candidate generator."
Separates "Actionable now," "Needs engineering check," and "Not transferable from current evidence," while explicitly excluding same-site stock and preventing double allocation.
"do not authorize transfers or recognize savings from this extract" provides a concrete safeguard against operational and financial risk.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: Rejects "Every semantic hit is transferable," "Description similarity proves identity," "Revision A and B are interchangeable," and "Global available_qty proves stock is free" with policy, identity, reservation, and freshness rationales.
"The issue is exclusively cross-site: questionable. Several requests also have apparent same-site inventory, suggesting the pilot should search local stock first."
Rejects additive candidate values by identifying competition for shared actuator and belt units.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Obtain a live donor-CMMS extract confirming on-hand, reservations and critical-spare status for each shortlisted part" is the highest-value freshness and availability check.
Also requests current request status, quote semantics, manufacturer numbers, revision mappings, receiving-site qualification, and transfer lead time/cost.

"With those fields, the $38,385.77 exact-spec pool can be converted from candidates into release decisions" links the evidence request to the decision, though the list could be more tightly prioritized into a minimal first query.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Actionable now: $0" and "No transfer is actionable now because donor stock is stale" are stronger than the evidence strictly supports: stale global data supports withholding authorization and downgrading certainty, not proof that no stock is currently transferable.

The detailed allocation totals and the $38,385.77 exact-spec pool are cited to broad row ranges rather than showing a reproducible request-by-request calculation, so those numerical results remain difficult to independently audit from the submission alone.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Some exact-spec candidates may already be transferable if local CMMS records, reservations, and critical-spare status are fresher than the 2026-06-26 global extract. Same-site inventory may also resolve some requests without cross-site transfer; therefore the evidence supports a hold-and-verify decision more strongly than a literal zero-availability conclusion.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a timestamped live CMMS query for the shortlisted exact manufacturer part numbers, joined to current open-request status, reservations, criticality, revision/UOM, and receiving-site qualification; then recompute the one-use allocation and report which candidates move from ceiling to actionable value.
